question: A nurse gets lower back pain after lifting heavy patients without help. What type of hazard is this?

question: Which eye condition is an absolute contraindication for anticholinergic medications?

question: Which behavioral change is a classic warning sign of potential substance abuse?

options.A: Neglecting work or school responsibilities
options.B: Consistent weight gain and healthy skin tone
options.C: An increased interest in family activities
options.D: Sudden improvement in daily sleep routines

question: What happens when a drug is tightly attached to blood proteins?

question: Why does a patient with acute gastroenteritis experience watery diarrhea?

options.B: Kidneys dump excess water directly into the large intestine
options.C: The stomach completely stops all digestive enzyme production
options.D: The liver stops producing bile needed to bind stool together

question: As a student nurse, what is one of the best things to watch out for when a patient starts a brand-new medication?

options.A: Stopping all routine laboratory blood tests to reduce patient stress
options.B: Ensuring the patient takes the medication strictly on an empty stomach
options.C: Monitoring for early subtle symptoms like fatigue, low fever, or itching
options.D: Teaching the patient how to calculate the cost of the prescription

explanation: Catching small warning signs early—like unusual tiredness or mild itching—helps you stop bigger organ damage before it starts. You're thinking like a real nurse! [learn more](GNS125_U5_T9#GNS125_U5_T9_h5)

question: How does constraint-induced movement therapy help a client with weakness on one side of their body?

options.A: It builds bulk muscle strength in the weak arm through heavy weightlifting.
options.B: It forces the brain to use the weak side by restricting the strong side.
options.C: It permanently immobilizes the strong side to prevent accidental injury.
options.D: It eliminates pain in the joints by keeping the limbs completely still.

explanation: By gently resting or blocking the good arm, we trick and encourage the brain to wake up and practice using the weaker side, boosting neuroplasticity! [learn more](GNS222_U3_T22#GNS222_U3_T22_h4)

question: A patient has a burn that looks leathery, dry, and white, and they feel no pain when it's touched. How would you chart this?

options.A: Deep partial-thickness burn
options.B: Superficial epidermal burn
options.C: Full-thickness burn
options.D: Superficial partial-thickness burn

question: Why does the nurse gently help the patient tuck their chin and knees tight together during this procedure?

options.C: To slow down the heart rate during the tap
options.D: To prevent the patient from biting their tongue

question: What is the best way for a nurse to encourage a traumatized widow to share her story?

options.A: Threatening to report her family to the police immediately
options.B: Insisting that she discuss the traumatic details in a crowded ward
options.C: Building trust through empathetic and confidential communication
options.D: Ignoring the emotional state and focusing only on vital signs

question: What is the very first thing a nurse should check before starting AROM with a patient?

question: Which nursing action helps calm a patient's fear of the unknown before a procedure?

options.A: Telling the patient not to ask any questions
options.B: Giving clear, simple explanations about what will happen
options.C: Leaving the room immediately after administering medication
options.D: Keeping all details secret until the exact moment of the test

question: Which of these is a critical warning sign that a pregnant woman must report straight away?

options.A: Occasional mild heartburn

options.C: Increased fatigue in the evening
options.D: Mild swelling in the ankles

question: What is the very first thing you must do if you realize you made a medication error?

options.A: Hide the medication chart so visitors do not notice the mistake

options.C: Blame the pharmacy department for supplying the wrong dose

explanation: Patient safety always comes first. Check your patient's vital signs and status immediately so you can handle any issues right away. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T2#GNS125_U3_T2_h5)

question: What happens when you cram way too much data into a single research table?

options.C: It becomes confusing and hard for readers to digest
options.D: It automatically makes all the calculations mathematically incorrect

question: Why are older adults especially vulnerable to bad reactions from medications?

options.A: Their liver and kidneys clear medications much more slowly
options.B: They always take their medicines at the wrong time of day
options.C: Their stomachs absorb all drugs faster than younger adults
options.D: They refuse to drink water when swallowing pills

question: Which sensory receptors deep in the skin are great at detecting deep pressure and heavy vibrations?

options.A: Pacinian corpuscles
options.B: Free nerve endings

options.D: Merkel discs

question: What part of a research article should a nurse examine to check the study design and sample size?

options.A: Methodology

question: Which action represents the correct use of alcohol-based hand rub?

options.C: Rinsing the hands with clean water right after applying the rub

question: How do most medications pass from a nursing mother's blood into her breast milk?

options.A: Cellular phagocytosis

question: Which chemical is most commonly used for high-level disinfection of heat-sensitive scopes?

question: Which sign is most typical in a patient who has damage to Broca's area?

options.A: Inability to hear or recognize spoken words from others

options.C: Complete paralysis of all four limbs on the right side

question: A community nurse notices a sudden rise in watery diarrhea cases in a village. What should they do first?

options.A: Advise villagers to stop drinking all liquids entirely
options.B: Close all local schools without notifying officials
options.C: Report the suspected cases immediately to public health authorities

question: Which tool do nurses commonly use to check a patient's ability to handle daily activities?

question: How is a dilator different from a regular feeding tube?

question: Why do the very first cell divisions (cleavage) happen without the embryo getting physically larger?

question: Why is Gallows traction only used for babies under two years old?

options.A: Toddlers over two refuse to lie flat

options.C: Heavier kids can lift their bodies and ruin the pull
options.D: Older children have bones that are too brittle

question: Which factor is most important for keeping a DRF cycle running successfully for years?

question: A nurse notices that people living near a stagnant river frequently catch malaria. What type of community is this?

question: What is the main goal of purposive sampling in qualitative studies?

question: Why are folk media like traditional drama and local songs so effective in rural communities?

question: In public health, what do we mean by 'food supply'?

question: Why do many breast cancer patients in Nigeria sadly arrive at the hospital with advanced stages?

question: A patient arrives at the ward struggling to breathe with swollen legs from heart failure. Which drug type is best to give right away for quick relief?

question: Why is home-based curative care important for patients with chronic conditions in rural communities?

question: Why is teaching a patient to keep a menstrual calendar a helpful nursing action?

question: What is the main goal of the Basel Convention?

question: Which practice should a nurse avoid when writing an incident report after a client falls off the bed?

options.C: Recording objective facts about how the client was found

question: What does it mean when a pathogen's 'portal of entry' matches its 'portal of exit'?

question: How does overall energy balance affect a patient's body weight over time?

question: When is the best time to record numbers for your monthly injection safety report?

question: What are the small bumps on the areola called that secrete a protective fluid?

question: What is the main goal of a 'root-cause analysis' when a mistake happens in a safe hospital?

options.A: Finding the exact junior staff member to blame for the incident

question: What do we mean in healthcare when we say 'the physical environment creates the disability'?

options.C: Bad weather directly causes permanent physical paralysis.

question: Which antibodies are naturally present in the plasma of a person with Type A blood?

question: A nurse wants to teach malaria prevention in a rural village with low literacy. What is the best design choice?

question: What size syringe should you use when trying to clear a blocked nasogastric tube?

question: Why is it smart to call the receiving hospital on the phone before sending an emergency patient?

question: What is the primary reason for tracking down and treating the sexual partners of an infected patient?

question: Why do premature babies often have trouble getting their ductus arteriosus to close?

question: Which of the following is NOT a standard preventive screening that nurses should promote for women's health?

question: What is the main job of Human Chorionic Gonadotropin (hCG) in early pregnancy?

question: Why do clinics use a daily attendance register alongside individual client files?

options.C: To quickly summarize daily clinic volume and service types
options.D: To track the personal financial income of clients

question: What is the main difference between isolation and quarantine?

question: In the labor ward, which practice is most important for preventing puerperal sepsis?

options.C: Administering intravenous fluids to every laboring woman

question: According to Kübler-Ross, what is usually the first stage of grief?

question: Why is 'trial and error' considered a risky problem-solving technique at the bedside?

question: Why is clear, informed consent so important before a couple starts IVF treatment?

question: Why is regular communication between nursing assistants and registered nurses so important in an SNF?

question: As a student nurse, what is your main personal duty when it comes to hospital waste guidelines?

question: Why do we need a clear research problem before starting any study?

question: How should a nurse handle personal religious beliefs when faced with an emergency PAC case?

options.A: By prioritizing the immediate life-saving care and treating the client without judgment
options.B: By transferring the patient to another facility without stabilization

question: Which Nigerian agency is in charge of regulating drugs and keeping track of adverse drug reactions?

question: A nurse places a naked newborn directly onto a cold metal scale. What type of heat loss is this?

options.A: Evaporation

question: What is the Hawthorne effect when observing staff nurses during audits?

options.A: A sudden spike in patient admissions during the rainy seasonal period
options.B: The mathematical formula used to calculate hospital bed occupancy rates
options.C: The rapid physical exhaustion nurses feel toward the end of a night shift
options.D: Staff changing their behavior temporarily because they know they are being watched

explanation: The Hawthorne effect reminds us that people naturally change how they work when they know someone is watching them closely. [learn more](GST321_U1_T19#GST321_U1_T19_h5)

question: Why do simple wellness talks or self-care lectures often fail to fix heavy nurse burnout on a hospital ward?

options.A: Nurses already know everything about relaxation techniques from basic school
options.B: Burnout is primarily an organizational issue caused by heavy workloads and poor support
options.C: Self-care workshops always increase the physical stress of working night shifts
options.D: Attending wellness lectures is legally considered part of unpaid overtime

explanation: Telling an exhausted nurse to 'just relax' won't solve unsafe staffing ratios, endless shifts, or lack of equipment. The root cause is the work environment itself! [learn more](GST321_U3_T6#GST321_U3_T6_h6)

question: A patient on a long-term central nervous system depressant asks if they can have a glass of wine with dinner. What should you say?

options.A: Drinking one small glass of wine will help the medication absorb faster into your bloodstream
options.B: Alcohol only interacts negatively with antibiotics, not with nervous system medications
options.C: You must avoid alcohol entirely because combining it with your medication can cause dangerous respiratory depression
options.D: You can safely drink alcohol as long as you take your medication two hours beforehand

question: A patient has heavy bleeding, bad cramps, an open cervix, and reports that some tissue has passed but parts are still inside. What is this called?

options.A: Threatened abortion
options.B: Missed abortion
options.C: Incomplete abortion
options.D: Septic abortion

question: Who on the subacute care team is usually responsible for assessing nutritional needs?

options.A: Occupational therapist
options.B: Physical therapist

options.D: Registered dietitian

question: What is the biggest perk of using a mixed methods design in nursing research?

options.A: It shortens the data collection phase to a single day
options.B: It provides a more complete picture by balancing numbers with human experience
options.C: It eliminates the need for any statistical calculations
options.D: It guarantees approval from all hospital ethical boards

explanation: Numbers tell us the 'how much,' but stories tell us the 'why.' Combining both gives us a much richer, more human understanding of healthcare challenges. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T1#GNS224_U1_T1_h6)

question: How do patriarchal power structures contribute to the continuation of harmful traditional practices?

options.A: By training nurses to perform traditional surgeries safely
options.B: By providing financial grants to families who follow customs

options.D: By enforcing rules that control female sexuality and behavior

question: What is the main job of the accessory organs in our digestive system?

options.A: To provide chemical secretions like enzymes and bile
options.B: To absorb all water from digested food materials
options.C: To physically push food forward using strong muscles
options.D: To serve as the primary storage tube for waste

question: Why do we regularly check liver function and platelet counts for a mum with severe preeclampsia?

options.A: To calculate her exact delivery date
options.B: To check for liver stress and HELLP syndrome
options.C: To check if the baby can breathe on its own
options.D: To find out the sex of the baby

explanation: Severe preeclampsia can sneak up on the liver and use up clotting cells (platelets). Watching these lab results helps us catch dangerous changes early! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T019#GNS226_U2_T019_h4)

question: A pregnant woman at a primary health clinic presents with facial swelling, blurred vision, and a blood pressure of 160/110 mmHg. What is the most appropriate nursing action?

options.A: Give her paracetamol tablets and ask her to wait
options.B: Advise her to drink plenty of palm wine and sleep
options.C: Send her home with instructions to rest for a week
options.D: Refer her urgently to a secondary or tertiary facility

explanation: These are signs of severe pre-eclampsia, which can quickly lead to deadly eclamptic seizures if not managed in a hospital. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T16#GNS225_U3_T16_h4)

question: Why can treating quarantine rules with harsh, heavy-handed punishments actually backfire?

options.A: It forces public health nurses to resign from their clinical positions

options.C: It drives infected people to hide their symptoms and avoid testing out of fear

question: Why must an endotracheal tube with an inflated cuff be placed in an unconscious patient before gastric lavage?

options.A: To keep the patient's mouth open wide during tube insertion

options.C: To deliver extra oxygen straight to the stomach lining
options.D: To protect the airway and stop fluid from entering the lungs

question: Why must nurses monitor a patient's blood pressure closely after they get spinal anesthesia?

options.A: Pain medication given intrathecally always increases heart rate

options.C: The body always produces extra blood volume after a spinal injection
options.D: Local anesthetics can block sympathetic nerves and cause significant low blood pressure

question: What is a major advantage of grassroots community-based interventions over top-down government bans?

options.C: They automatically override all existing national laws
options.D: They cost zero financial resources to plan and execute

question: What is the main reason for placing a Word catheter after draining a Bartholin cyst?

options.C: To keep the new drainage opening open so a fresh duct can form
options.D: To permanently stop all fluid production in the body

question: How does eating too much salt contribute to high blood pressure?

options.A: It causes fluid retention which increases total blood volume.
options.B: It directly weakens the heart valves causing backflow.
options.C: It thickens the red blood cells so they cannot move easily.
options.D: It instantly melts the protective lining inside the veins.

question: Why do patients with these disorders sometimes show sudden changes like anger or unfriendliness (apathy)?

options.B: Inadequate daily fluid intake causing mild dehydration
options.C: Normal psychological adjustment to aging processes
options.D: Damage to frontal lobe structures controlling mood and behavior

question: During which stage of HIV do patients often get a sudden spike in virus levels and flu-like signs?

options.D: Terminal malignant stage

question: Which of the following is a clear indication for starting dialysis in acute renal failure?

question: What happens during a chemical antagonism between two substances?

question: What is the most common symptom of a pinworm infection?

question: Which population group often develops metabolic health risks at much lower BMI thresholds?

question: A patient asks how eating more vegetables and whole grains helps their heart. What is the best nursing explanation?

question: A nurse notices morning shift surgical patients report less pain than evening ones. Why is this a good research problem?

options.B: It proves that evening nurses are performing their duties incorrectly

question: When is the right time to suction a patient who is on a ventilator?

question: How do painful abscesses and bacterial infections usually happen after an injection?

question: Which of these is usually the first noticeable sign that an adult is getting dehydrated?

question: A mother is worried that routine immunizations will make her baby sick with a fever. What is the best way to reassure her?

question: What is the primary purpose of vasopressor medications in treating shock?

options.C: To slow down a dangerously rapid heart rate

question: What immediate action should a nurse take if a quarantined person develops a sudden fever?

question: Why must a patient finish all their antibiotics even if their skin looks completely better?

question: Which lifestyle habit directly helps improve pelvic blood circulation and mood?

question: A patient stays completely quiet during a health talk. What is a common mistake nurses make when interpreting this?

question: How is the BCG vaccine usually given to a newborn?

question: What ethical principle ensures that a patient has the right to make their own healthcare decisions without pressure?

question: A nurse is checking a 15-year-old girl who feels very tired, dizzy, and has pale nail beds. What is the best first step to take?

question: What is the typical normal oxygen saturation range for a healthy adult breathing room air?

question: Why is a bedside double-check with two nurses a must before starting a blood transfusion?

question: Where should used lancets go immediately after a finger prick?

question: What happens during a uterine perforation?

question: How much extra stockinette length should generally be cut beyond the planned cast area?

question: Which structure travels inside the spermatic cord along with nerves and blood vessels?

question: What does healthy pink or red granulation tissue tell you about a wound?

question: A patient arrives sweating heavily with thick makeup on their forehead. What should you do for their temperature?

question: At what age does a baby usually receive their first dose of the Pentavalent vaccine?

question: How does the bone underneath usually react once the protective cartilage wears away?

question: A ward manager notices missed medication doses and sloppy handovers. What is the most likely underlying issue?

options.C: Excessively high patient satisfaction survey scores

question: How can a nurse best reassure a patient who has mild pregnancy nausea?

options.C: Eating large meals will cure the queasiness within hours.
options.D: The symptoms will disappear completely by the second week.

explanation: Mums worry the baby isn't eating enough. Letting them know that mild early nausea won't hurt their little one brings great peace of mind! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T011#GNS226_U2_T011_h7)

question: Which of these is a MISTAKE when getting a patient ready for a digital blood pressure check?

options.A: Making sure both of the patient's feet are flat on the floor
options.B: Asking the patient to stay quiet while the machine runs
options.C: Allowing the patient to keep a thick sweater on with the cuff rolled over it
options.D: Ensuring the patient rests quietly for five minutes beforehand

explanation: Always put the cuff directly on bare skin! Thick clothing or tight rolling can pinch the arm and mess up your numbers. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T1#GNS212_U4_T1_h4)

question: What is a fixed cost in a healthcare unit?

options.A: The variable wages paid to casual registry nurses
options.B: A cost that changes daily based on medication usage
options.C: An expense that stays the same regardless of patient numbers
options.D: An emergency fund used only for unexpected equipment breakdowns

explanation: Fixed costs stay stable month after month, no matter if your ward is overflowing with patients or half-empty! [learn more](GST321_U4_T3#GST321_U4_T3_h3)

question: How long can the common Copper T 380A IUD stay in place?

options.A: For the rest of the woman's life
options.B: Exactly 1 to 2 years
options.C: A maximum of 6 months
options.D: Up to 10 to 12 years

explanation: The Copper T 380A is a real champion for long-term family planning—it's approved to stay in safely for up to a decade! [learn more](GNS226_U6_T015#GNS226_U6_T015_h3)

question: Which detail must be included in the nursing documentation after a patient dies?

options.A: The financial status of the patient's family
options.B: The exact time death was pronounced
options.C: The names of all nurses working on the next shift
options.D: The exact cause of the underlying disease

explanation: The exact time of death pronouncement by the doctor is a legal requirement that must be documented in the nursing notes. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T10#GNS221_U4_T10_h6)

question: A teenage boy asks why his voice is cracking and getting deeper. What is the cause?

options.A: Weakening of the throat muscles during physical exercise
options.B: Temporary irritation of the airway from rapid lung growth
options.C: Growth and thickening of the vocal cords due to testosterone
options.D: Swelling of the tonsils caused by common adolescent infections

explanation: Correct! As testosterone levels rise, the larynx and vocal cords grow larger and thicker, which naturally drops the pitch of the voice. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T8#GNS311_U1_T8_h3)

question: What gets squeezed flat against the tunica albuginea to trap blood inside the penis?

options.A: Subtunical venules
options.B: Dorsal nerve fibers
options.C: Cavernous arteries
options.D: Urethral glands

question: Why must a scrub nurse know the exact name and purpose of every surgical instrument?

options.A: It is a legal requirement for writing the patient's record
options.B: It helps the doctor finish the operation without speaking
options.C: It prevents prolonged surgery and accidental tissue damage
options.D: It stops the instruments from rusting during the procedure

explanation: Knowing your tools allows you to anticipate the surgeon's needs quickly, keeping the operation safe and efficient. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T9#GNS123_U5_T9_h1)

question: Why should you still talk and explain procedures to a sedated patient on a ventilator?

options.A: It satisfies the legal requirement for written informed consent
options.B: It helps the mechanical ventilator synchronize with the patient's heart
options.C: Unconscious or sedated patients may still perceive and process sound
options.D: Hospital regulations require talking to every patient on a machine

explanation: Hearing is often the last sense to go. Explaining what you are doing is a kind, human act that helps soothe fear and confusion. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T10#GNS321_U2_T10_h8)

question: What is the most important safety rule when changing a patient's tracheostomy neck ties?

options.A: Have an assistant hold the tube in place
options.B: Do it quickly without washing hands
options.C: Inflate the cuff to maximum pressure
options.D: Remove the inner cannula permanently

explanation: Always have a partner hold the tube securely during tie changes. One good cough can pop the tube right out! [learn more](GNS213_U2_T14#GNS213_U2_T14_h4)

question: Why is a pregnant woman living in a remote rural Nigerian village at the highest risk for maternal mortality?

options.A: Strict adherence to modern medical guidelines
options.B: A higher biological predisposition to bleeding
options.C: Geographic isolation and limited access to emergency obstetric care
options.D: Overuse of specialized antenatal clinics

explanation: Distance matters! Living far from a clinic means severe delays in getting emergency help when complications arise. This is a huge challenge in rural healthcare. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T012#GNS226_U1_T012_h2)

question: At what point does the second stage of labour officially start?

options.A: When the placenta is delivered
options.B: When the cervix is completely dilated
options.C: When the amniotic membranes rupture
options.D: When contractions become painful and regular

explanation: You nailed it! The second stage begins right when the cervix is fully open at 10 cm and ends when the baby is born. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T006#GNS226_U3_T006_h5)

question: How do medications interact with our cells?

options.A: By permanently replacing vital organs with chemical substitutes
options.B: By modifying or blocking already existing cellular activities
options.C: By changing the basic genetic code of the target organ
options.D: By destroying diseased cells and generating brand new tissues

explanation: Great job! Think of drugs as little keys that speed up, slow down, or block processes your body already knows how to do. [learn more](GNS125_U1_T3#GNS125_U1_T3_h1)

question: What does 'youth participation' mean in healthcare settings?

options.A: Allowing teenagers to clean the hospital wards daily
options.B: Making teenagers work as full-time hospital receptionists
options.C: Requiring youth to pay for community medical bills
options.D: Involving adolescents in planning and evaluating health programs

explanation: You got it! Youth participation means letting young people have a voice in shaping the programs meant to serve them. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T17#GNS312_U3_T17_h7)

question: A 14-year-old girl is growing fast and has started her monthly periods. How does this affect her food and nutrient needs?

options.A: She only needs extra water and no other dietary changes
options.B: Her nutritional demands decrease because her body is slowing down
options.C: Her nutritional demands remain exactly the same as childhood
options.D: Her nutritional demands increase significantly to support growth and blood loss

explanation: Exactly! Rapid body growth plus monthly blood loss means she needs more energy, protein, and key minerals to stay strong and healthy. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T010#GNS227_U2_T010_h2)

question: Which common medication class is one of the top triggers for hospital-acquired anaphylaxis?

options.A: Antihypertensive drugs
options.B: Inhaled bronchodilators
options.C: Penicillin antibiotics
options.D: Potassium supplements

explanation: Penicillin and other beta-lactam drugs are famous culprits. Always double-check a patient's allergy history before giving them! [learn more](GST114_U4_T9#GST114_U4_T9_h2)

question: Which nerve pathway carries fine touch and vibration signals all the way up to the brain?

options.A: Spinothalamic pathway
options.B: Pyramidal motor tract
options.C: Dorsal column-medial lemniscal pathway
options.D: Corticospinal tract

explanation: Don't let the long name scare you! The dorsal column-medial lemniscal pathway is just the main highway for detailed touch and vibration. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T11#GNS211_U4_T11_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT a common reason why infectious diseases end up underreported in clinics?

options.A: Ignorance of the list of notifiable diseases
options.B: Fear of blame or administrative punishment by management
options.C: Excessive availability of rapid diagnostic testing kits
options.D: Heavy clinical workloads and lack of reporting forms

explanation: Great job! Having plenty of testing kits would actually make reporting easier, not harder. Heavy workloads and fear are the real culprits behind underreporting. [learn more](GST114_U2_T20#GST114_U2_T20_h8)

question: What are the three Greek root words that make up the word epidemiology?

options.A: Eco, demos, and therapy
options.B: Epi, genos, and lysis
options.C: Epi, demos, and logos
options.D: Endo, pathos, and bios

explanation: You've got this! The term breaks down nicely: epi means 'upon', demos means 'people', and logos means 'study'. Together, they form the study of health events affecting populations. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T1#GNS313_U1_T1_h1)

question: A toddler arrives at the emergency unit suddenly drooling, making high-pitched breathing sounds (stridor), and very restless, but has no cough. What should you do first?

options.A: Keep the child calm and avoid invasive examinations
options.B: Immediately force the child to lie flat for an X-ray
options.C: Attempt to visualize the vocal cords with a tongue depressor
options.D: Administer oral fluids immediately to soothe the throat

explanation: This sounds like epiglottitis! If you upset or cry the child, their swollen airway can snap shut completely. Keep them calm in their mother's arms and don't force anything into their mouth. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T3#GNS212_U2_T3_h5)

question: How do most drugs cross cell membranes when they are being absorbed?

options.A: Pinocytosis
options.B: Osmotic pressure
options.C: Passive diffusion
options.D: Active transport

explanation: Most drugs just cruise right through cell membranes via passive diffusion—moving smoothly from an area of high concentration to low concentration without using up any energy! [learn more](GNS125_U1_T4#GNS125_U1_T4_h2)

question: Why is spousal communication often encouraged in Nigerian family planning counselling?

options.A: Partner support helps improve long-term contraceptive adherence
options.B: Nigerian law prohibits women from buying drugs independently
options.C: Men are the only ones who experience contraceptive side effects
options.D: Husbands must legally sign all medical forms in public hospitals

explanation: When partners understand and support the chosen method, the client faces less household conflict and continues use more successfully. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T022#GNS226_U6_T022_h8)

question: What happens to chemical indicator strips when they are exposed to the correct sterilization conditions?

options.A: Their weight and density
options.B: Their color
options.C: Their physical length
options.D: Their magnetic polarity

explanation: Spot on! Special dyes in the strip change color to let you know the correct temperature or chemical levels were reached inside the load. [learn more](GST114_U2_T9#GST114_U2_T9_h7)

question: What is a key feature that makes a tertiary health facility unique?

options.A: It only handles uncomplicated outpatient malaria cases
options.B: It is the first point of contact in a rural village
options.C: It provides basic immunization only
options.D: It serves as a center for training and medical research

explanation: Tertiary hospitals (like our teaching hospitals) do double duty: they provide advanced patient care while training future healthcare heroes and conducting medical research. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T2#GNS112_U2_T2_h4)

question: What happens if you manage to disrupt just one single link in the chain of infection?

options.A: The pathogen automatically changes into a harmless virus
options.B: The susceptible host becomes permanently immune
options.C: The infection process is completely stopped
options.D: The reservoir doubles its reproductive rate

explanation: Brilliant! The chain needs every single link to stay connected. Break just one, and the disease is stopped in its tracks. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T9#GNS324_U6_T9_h2)

question: A patient is rushed in with pinpoint pupils, severe sleepiness, and very slow breathing after a drug overdose. Which antidote do you expect the doctor to order?

options.A: Atropine
options.B: Flumazenil
options.C: Naloxone
options.D: Calcium gluconate

question: What is the single biggest risk factor for developing osteoarthritis?

options.A: Living in cold climates
options.B: Advanced age
options.C: Eating too much red meat
options.D: Cracking your knuckles

explanation: Getting older is the primary risk factor because joint cartilage naturally weakens and loses its shock-absorbing ability over time. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T14#GNS222_U1_T14_h2)

question: Which grade of moulding describes skull bones that overlap firmly but can still be separated by finger pressure?

options.A: Grade 3 moulding
options.B: Grade 1 moulding

options.D: Grade 0 moulding

explanation: Grade 1 means the bones overlap slightly but remain reducible with gentle pressure. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T14#GNS121_U6_T14_h3)

question: What common health problem can happen when cultural food taboos stop pregnant women from eating meat and eggs?

options.A: Gestational diabetes mellitus
options.B: Excessive fetal birth weight
options.C: Rapid maternal weight gain
options.D: Severe iron-deficiency anemia

explanation: Brilliant! When expecting mothers miss out on protein and iron-rich foods, their bodies struggle to make enough red blood cells, leading to anemia. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T1#GNS312_U1_T1_h4)

question: Which of these is NOT a sign that a patient is lacking fluid (fluid volume deficit)?

options.B: Dry mucous membranes
options.C: Bounding peripheral pulses
options.D: Concentrated dark urine

question: Why do nurses need to check a patient's other medications when starting an antiparasitic drug that goes through the liver?

options.A: Liver enzymes completely neutralize the therapeutic effect of all parasites
options.B: Patients with liver issues cannot absorb any form of topical cream
options.C: Many antiparasitic drugs are metabolized by liver enzymes, altering blood levels
options.D: Hepatic enzymes prevent gastrointestinal side effects entirely

question: When a study is called 'empirical,' what kind of information is the researcher using?

options.A: Ancient cultural traditions and habits

options.C: Strictly theoretical guesses without testing
options.D: Observable and measurable real-world data

question: A nurse suspects a young househelp brought to the clinic is being trafficked. What should the nurse do first?

options.C: Send the child home and report the incident to the local market union
options.D: Confront the accompanying employer aggressively in the waiting room

question: Which form of a drug molecule passes most easily across biological cell membranes?

options.A: Ionized
options.B: Conjugated
options.C: Unionized
options.D: Protein-bound

explanation: Unionized (un-charged) drug molecules are more fat-friendly (lipophilic), helping them slip smoothly across cell membranes. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T1#GNS125_U5_T1_h4)

question: Which leadership style is best when a patient suddenly collapses and needs emergency resuscitation on the ward?

options.A: Transformational
options.B: Autocratic
options.C: Democratic
options.D: Laissez-faire

explanation: In an emergency, there's no time to debate. An autocratic (directive) style saves crucial time because one person clearly gives fast instructions. [learn more](GST321_U1_T14#GST321_U1_T14_h3)

question: A patient is going home with a new antibiotic prescription. What crucial tip must you give them?

options.A: Stop taking the capsules the moment your fever breaks

options.C: Complete the full prescribed course even if symptoms disappear early
options.D: Store all antibiotic bottles in the direct sunlight on your veranda

question: Why is a severe haemorrhage dangerous to human tissues?

options.A: It speeds up the heart rate until the heart muscle rests
options.B: It floods the organs with excess waste products
options.C: It starves tissues of oxygen and vital nutrients
options.D: It causes an immediate and dangerous rise in blood pressure

question: A patient on a new BP medication feels dizzy when standing up. What should you do first as the nurse?

options.C: Advise the patient to stop taking the medication immediately at home
options.D: Instruct the patient to rise slowly and report symptoms to the provider

question: Why is teaming up with local community groups important for family care plans?

options.C: Government laws make it illegal to work without church approval
options.D: International agencies handle all treatments for poor kids

question: Why do many pregnant women complain of lower back pain and wobbly joints?

options.A: Excess weight causes rapid cartilage breakdown in the knees

options.C: The growing fetus puts direct pressure on the spinal vertebrae
options.D: Calcium is actively pulled out of the joints to build fetal bones

question: What is the standard diagnostic test used to confirm onchocerciasis?

options.A: Chest X-ray imaging
options.B: Bone marrow biopsy
options.C: Stool microscopy for ova
options.D: Skin snip microscopy

question: Why is the epiglottis such an important little flap in your throat?

options.A: It separates the nasal cavity from the oral cavity

options.C: It prevents food and liquid from entering the trachea during swallowing

question: What is the primary benefit of enrolling a patient in a structured cardiac rehabilitation program?

options.A: Providing a surgical alternative to coronary artery bypass grafting
options.B: Improving overall physical conditioning and reducing future heart risks
options.C: Ensuring the patient never has to take prescription medications again
options.D: Eliminating the need for routine follow-up visits with the cardiologist

explanation: Cardiac rehabilitation helps patients regain strength, manage risk factors, lower stress, and significantly reduce the likelihood of future cardiac events. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T13#GNS213_U1_T13_h6)

question: How does partnering with schools help improve childhood immunization rates?

options.A: It forces teachers to administer complex injectable vaccines
options.B: It allows health workers to check vaccination cards and catch up on missed doses
options.C: It ensures that children never catch common colds at home
options.D: It replaces the need for infant clinics at primary health centers

explanation: Schools provide a structured setting where health workers can easily review children's immunization records and administer catch-up vaccines. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T71#GNS214_U1_T71_h7)

question: Which of these is NOT a common cause of high potassium (hyperkalemia)?

options.A: Taking medications that hold onto potassium

options.D: Breakdown of damaged muscle tissue

question: Why is it so helpful to introduce psychological support early after a degenerative diagnosis?

options.A: It helps patients adapt before severe cognitive decline sets in

options.C: It stops the physical degeneration from spreading to organs
options.D: It guarantees complete recovery from emotional distress

explanation: Starting early means patients can still clearly express their thoughts and take part in planning their own care. Great nursing insight to keep in mind! [learn more](GNS222_U4_T18#GNS222_U4_T18_h1)

question: What is the main difference between airborne and droplet transmission?

options.A: Droplet particles can travel for miles across different cities

options.C: Airborne droplet nuclei stay suspended in the air much longer
options.D: Airborne particles only spread through contaminated drinking water

explanation: Airborne transmission involves tiny particles that stay in the air and travel far, whereas large droplets quickly fall to the ground. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T5#GNS123_U4_T5_h4)

question: What are the two primary functions of the ovaries during this monthly cycle?

options.A: Maturing follicles and producing sex hormones
options.B: Digesting fats and making red blood cells
options.C: Producing urine and filtering blood cells
options.D: Storing waste and regulating body temperature

question: When should a nurse expect a patient to be switched to a second-line HIV regimen?

options.C: After the patient has taken the first drugs for exactly one year

question: Which of the following is a common myth associated with modern contraceptives?

options.D: They cure all known infectious diseases

question: What do we call those tiny, pinpoint red or purple spots caused by tiny bleeding vessels under the skin?

question: A clinic treats all teenagers fairly, without any bias based on religion or wealth. Which core principle is this?

options.A: Equity
options.B: Speed
options.C: Isolation
options.D: Specialization

explanation: Correct! Equity means fairness and zero discrimination—every young person gets the care they need regardless of background. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T17#GNS312_U3_T17_h3)

question: Why is proper nutrition especially critical for children attending day care centres?

options.A: It eliminates the need for any physical exercise routines
options.B: It replaces the need for routine childhood immunizations
options.C: It guarantees that children will never catch a common cold
options.D: It supports both physical growth and cognitive development

explanation: Balanced nutrition provides the essential energy and nutrients required for growing bodies and developing brains during early childhood. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T7#GNS225_U4_T7_h5)

question: How does political interference usually affect public health spending in Nigeria?

options.A: Projects are sometimes placed where politicians want rather than where health needs are greatest
options.B: Corruption is completely eradicated from hospital boards
options.C: Budgets are automatically increased to match international health targets
options.D: Hospitals receive surplus medical equipment in every rural ward

explanation: Sometimes health facilities are built to score political points in certain areas rather than going where the actual health data shows they are needed. [learn more](GST322_U3_T3#GST322_U3_T3_h6)

question: A patient recovering from a leg fracture is frustrated and feels like giving up. Which rehabilitation goal addresses this?

options.B: Eliminating the need for any future physical therapy
options.C: Promoting psychological adjustment and coping
options.D: Replacing lost joint cartilage with synthetic tissue

question: Why is an iodine-based contrast dye sometimes given during a brain CT scan?

options.B: To lower the patient's blood pressure
options.C: To protect the kidneys from radiation

question: A patient with an enlarged prostate hasn't peed in eight hours and has severe lower belly pain. What should you do first?

question: What is the main goal of a Drug Revolving Fund (DRF) in a hospital?

options.B: To provide free medical treatments to all vulnerable populations
options.C: To pay the monthly salaries of clinical and administrative staff
options.D: To generate excess profit for hospital infrastructure development

question: Which symptom usually goes hand-in-hand with excessive flatulence?

options.D: Yellow discoloration of the skin

question: What is the primary purpose of breaking any link in the chain of infection?

options.C: To cure a chronic illness without using antibiotics
options.D: To stop the transmission of infectious diseases

question: A patient starting HIV treatment is worried about forgetting their daily pills. What is a helpful nursing action?

question: What kind of trouble does a nurse face for leaving their duty post without official permission?

options.A: An automatic promotion to a higher administrative grade level
options.B: A commendation letter from the hospital management board
options.C: Immediate conversion of the absence into paid study leave
options.D: Severe administrative penalties for gross misconduct

explanation: Absconding or leaving work without approval is treated as truancy and attracts serious disciplinary action. Always secure your leave first! [learn more](GST321_U10_T1#GST321_U10_T1_h5)

question: Which complication happens most directly when sharp metal objects are pushed into the uterus?

options.A: Chronic hypertension and peripheral edema
options.B: Uterine perforation and severe hemorrhage
options.C: Allergic rhinitis and skin rashes
options.D: Renal stone formation and bladder spasms

explanation: Unskilled hands using sharp instruments can easily pierce the muscular wall of the uterus, causing heavy internal bleeding. That's a major medical emergency! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T003#GNS226_U5_T003_h4)

question: What must a nurse do before changing how they care for patients based on a new research paper?

options.A: Carefully check the study's validity and methods first
options.B: Wait ten whole years before taking any action
options.C: Just assume it's true because it was printed in a magazine
options.D: Ask every single hospital patient for their permission

explanation: Evidence-based practice means we don't just follow every new trend blindly; we appraise the research to make sure it's solid and safe. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T26#GNS224_U1_T26_h7)

question: Why is gender equity often necessary before gender equality can be truly achieved?

options.A: Equity provides tailored support to overcome existing social disadvantages
options.B: Equality is harmful and should be replaced entirely by equity
options.C: Equity means treating all patients with the exact same standard protocol
options.D: Equity ensures that biological sex differences are completely erased

explanation: Because historical inequalities put certain groups behind, equity steps in with customized help so everyone has a fair chance to reach an equal outcome. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T1#GNS312_U4_T1_h6)

question: A patient vomits heavily during a cardiac arrest. What should the nurse grab right away?

options.A: The suction catheter and canister
options.B: The laryngoscope handle
options.C: The bag-valve-mask resuscitator
options.D: The endotracheal tube stylet

question: A client suddenly shows a change in pupil size and a dropping GCS score. What does this most likely indicate?

options.A: Normal recovery from head trauma
options.B: An allergic reaction to hospital food
options.C: A sudden drop in body temperature
options.D: Rising pressure inside the skull

question: As a community health nurse, why must you look at environmental factors when assessing a patient's stress?

options.A: Environmental triggers are the only proven cause of mental illness
options.B: External pressures like security and poverty often drive individual stress
options.C: Individual counseling works without knowing the community background
options.D: Nurses are required to fix bad roads and public infrastructure

explanation: An individual's stress rarely happens in a vacuum. Shared hardships like poverty or safety issues play a huge role in how they feel. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T6#GNS313_U3_T6_h4)

question: Which of these is NOT a core principle of a Drug Revolving Fund?

options.A: Maintaining strict financial accountability and transparency
options.B: Selling pharmaceuticals at affordable prices to patients
options.C: Maximizing high profit margins for hospital expansion
options.D: Ensuring constant availability of essential medicines

question: Which vitamin is synthesized in the skin when exposed to sunlight?

options.A: Vitamin C
options.B: Vitamin D
options.C: Vitamin K
options.D: Vitamin A

question: Which organelle is responsible for producing most of the cell's energy in the form of ATP?

options.A: Lysosome
options.B: Rough endoplasmic reticulum
options.C: Golgi apparatus
options.D: Mitochondria

explanation: Mitochondria convert nutrients into usable cellular energy (ATP), earning them the title of cellular powerhouses. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T5#GNS111_U1_T5_h3)

question: A rural health clinic in Nigeria runs out of basic antibiotics due to weak local distribution. Which national strategy is failing in this specific instance?

options.A: The regulation of surgical equipment manufacturing standards
options.B: The curriculum used to train primary school teachers
options.C: The Essential Drug Policy supply chain and distribution network
options.D: The enforcement of international luxury hotel taxation

question: What is the normal job of tumor suppressor genes in our bodies?

options.A: To stimulate rapid cell growth during injury
options.B: To supply blood vessels directly to growing tissues
options.C: To carry oxygen to rapidly dividing cancer cells
options.D: To slow down cell division and repair damaged DNA

question: What is a major safety worry for a patient who has lost feeling (protective sensation) in their arms or legs?

options.B: Excessive verbal outbursts
options.C: Sudden loss of hearing
options.D: Burns and pressure injuries

explanation: When patients can't feel hot, cold, or pressure, they won't pull away from a hot stove or shift their weight, leaving their skin wide open to quiet injuries and sores. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T22#GNS222_U3_T22_h3)
